punchline: The whale needed two blows and about ten minutes; the first mate spent them saving compasses.
thirty_sec: In November 1820 the whaleship Essex was stove in by a sperm whale, twice, far out in the Pacific. First mate Owen Chase says the whole thing took no more than ten minutes. In that time the crew saved two quadrants, navigation books and two compasses, then cut through the deck for six hundred pounds of bread. Twenty men went into three open boats, and the instruments were what told them where they were.
